question: Should schema-valid `sessions.list` requests above 1,000 now be intentionally clamped to a paginated first page, or must the existing direct-RPC behavior remain available?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically small and proof-positive, but it changes a public gateway result for inputs the protocol currently accepts without an upper bound. Existing sibling clamps do not establish that this endpoint’s clients may be truncated.

options.title: Adopt the capped paging contract
options.body: Approve the 1,000-row ceiling, then rebase and make the gateway/protocol compatibility expectation explicit with focused client-facing coverage.

options.title: Preserve existing RPC semantics
options.body: Keep `sessions.list` unbounded for direct clients and pursue a narrower tool-side or separately designed resource-protection measure.

recommendation.title: Adopt the capped paging contract
recommendation.body: Approve the 1,000-row ceiling, then rebase and make the gateway/protocol compatibility expectation explicit with focused client-facing coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged adjacent gateway-limit work is the strongest available ownership signal for aligning or distinguishing this contract.
